title: Drawing I
description: Fundamentals of observational and subjective drawing in a variety of media.

title: Two Dimensional Design
description: Fundamentals of elements and organizing principles of two dimensional design to include basic color theory in a variety of media.

title: Drawing II
description: Line and value in drawing; emphasis on structure and proportion, sketching, gesture, and contour drawing.

title: Three Dimensional Design
description: Fundamentals of elements and organizing principles of three dimensional design to include a variety of media and processes.

title: Artists and Designers in Real Time
description: Overview of professional practice in contemporary art, design, art history. Readings and discussion contextualize presentation topics.

title: Photography and Visual Communication
description: Visual expression and literacy using photographic concepts and media.

title: Modern Making
description: Contemporary object design and production. Introduction to techniques, processes, and technologies used in craft, design, and creative industries.

title: Visual Presentation
description: Design drawing techniques including interior presentation drawings, interior detailing, architectural drafting, and lettering. Tools and materials used in the design professions.

title: Introduction to Art
description: An illustrated lecture course dealing with the meaning of art derived from an investigation of the principles of art. Designed to increase the understanding and appreciation of art.

title: Life Drawing I
description: Drawing from the nude model.

title: Painting I
description: Pictorial composition and techniques of painting.

title: Printmaking I
description: Introduction and exploration of basic printmaking media. Emphasis on aesthetic and technical processes in intaglio, lithography, relief and serigraphy.

title: Visual Odyssey through Comics and Sequential Media
description: Techniques and methodologies for applying visual tools such as drawing, photography, and video to the telling of culturally relevant stories.

title: Sculpture I
description: Introduction and experimentation of basic sculpture ideas, methods, and materials.

title: Material Studies in Craft and Design
description: Material processes, craftspersonship, and design strategies for functional objects in various materials such as clay, wood, and metal.

title: Funadamentals of Woodworking
description: An introduction to the fundamentals of woodworking and the basic tools and safe operations of the wood shop.
notes: Recommended before taking ART 323 and for non-majors.

title: Introduction to Ceramics
description: Introduction to methods of building, glazing, and firing of handbuilt and wheel-thrown forms.

title: Jewelry and Metalwork Fundamentals
description: Introduction to design and construction of jewelry. Basic fabrication and elementary surface embellishment techniques in non-ferrous metals, emphasizing the use of the elements and principles of design.

title: Fundamentals of Digital Media
description: Principles of digital media used in visual communication.

title: The House and Its Environment
description: Architecture, interior design, landscape and city planning for forming the physical and aesthetic environment.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Fundamentals of Digital Design and Fabrication
description: Fundamentals of digital design, presentation, and fabrication for artists and designers.

title: Environmental Presentation
description: Methods, materials, and tools of the professional environmental designer stressing art principles.

title: Introduction to Art History I
description: Global art development in art, architecture, and design from prehistory to the 15th century.

title: Introduction to Art History II
description: Global art development in art, architecture, and design from the 15th century to the modern period.

title: African, Asian, and Oceanic Art
description: Art, architecture, and design of African, Asian, and Oceanic regions from prehistory to the modern period.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Screen Printing Studio
description: Traditional and experimental processes and techniques of screen printing to include design development and artistic image making through a cohesive body of work utilizing the medium.

title: Furniture and Wood I
description: Introduction to the design and construction of functional objects and furniture. Basic techniques in woodworking and joinery.
notes: Recommend ART 223 before ART 323 for non-majors

title: Ceramics I - Wheel Throwing
description: Introduction to methods of building, glazing, and firing wheel-thrown vessel forms

title: Ceramics I - Handbuilding
description: Introduction to methods of building, glazing, and firing handbuilt forms

title: Jewelry and Metalwork I
description: Creative design and construction of jewelry and small objects. Techniques in three-dimensional forming, complex fabrication, and surface manipulation, in non-ferrous metals, emphasizing conceptual development, personal expression, and reflection.
notes: Suggested additional preparation: ART 220 or ART 231 (recommended)

title: Digital Photography I
description: Visual communication and expression using digital photographic media and digital imaging techniques.

title: Graphic Design II
description: Visual problem-solving skills through a variety of design methods. Conceptual thinking, experimentation, and research in design for print and screen-based media. Study of content, form, signs, and symbols.

title: Typography II
description: Typographic issues pertaining to concept, expression, and meaning using design tools for development of printed and screen-based media. Implementation of narrative and time-based typographic systems.

title: Expressive Typography
description: History, process, and technology of relief printing and experimental concepts using digital technologies, moveable type and photographic processes to create individual and collaborative designs that integrate image and text.

title: Illustration I
description: Visual notation, sketching, representational drawing, and visual translation related to art and design.

title: Design for the Internet I
description: Creative and practical applications of interactive visual communication for presentation on the Internet.

title: History of Graphic Design
description: Evolution of graphic communication from prehistory through postmodern design and the digital revolution.

title: Introduction to Book Arts
description: Terminology, tools, materials, and reproduction processes related to the making of books; historical and contemporary book structures; and development of content in the form of image and text.

title: The House and Its Environment
description: Architecture, interior design, landscape, and city planning for forming the physical and aesthetic environment, its simplicities and complexities.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Three Dimensional Digital Media
description: Design communication utilizing digital media as it relates to three-dimensional objects and spatial environments.

title: Aesthetics of Architectural Design: Concepts and Practice
description: Addresses fundamental issues of aesthetics related to architecture, interiors, and design-emphasizing modern and contemporary design concerning socioeconomic and multicultural issues.

title: Light and Color: Designing for Interior Wellbeing
description: Investigates how light and color design elements affect human experience and interior wellbeing. A study in local and international environmental design solutions including recreational, educational and health care facilities.

title: Methods and Materials for Sustainable Built Environments
description: Codes, contractual issues, design practices, legal liabilities, professional ethics, and project management. Selection of materials and methods of installation.

title: World Art in Contemporary Life
description: World art and technology from ancient to post modern era and their relationship to contemporary culture and life. Gallery visits required.

title: Medieval Art
description: Development of painting, sculpture, and architecture from time of Constantine through Gothic period.

title: Creative Coding
description: Introduction to computer programming and computational thinking in service of creating generative and interactive art. Emphasis on play and experimentation as critical approaches to creative problem solving. No prior coding experience required.

title: Art Education History and Practice
description: History and theory of art education. Role of art in child and adolescent development, art heritage, diversity and equity in art education and teaching methodologies.

title: Art Field Experience with Elementary and Middle School Students
description: Prepares pre-service teachers to be effective educators of visual art. Field observation, class lectures on lesson planning, instructional techniques, and strategies for teaching art to elementary school and middle school students.

title: Art Field Experience with High School Students
description: Prepares pre-service teachers to be effective educators of visual art. Field observation, class lectures on lesson planning, instructional techniques, and strategies for teaching art to high school students.

title: Art for Elementary School Teacher
description: A design-crafts course that explores in depth materials and processes primarily used by the elementary school teacher.

title: Writing about Art and Design
description: Students will research and read a variety of approaches to writing about art and design, read contemporary writing on art and design, participate in peer editing and dialogue about one another’s writing, and collaborate to create an original publication.

title: Life Drawing II
description: Drawing the nude model.

title: Painting II
description: Concepts that enhance basic painting principles and a broad range of painting issues.

title: Experimental Processes in Art
description: Structure in picture making.

title: Film Photography I
description: Black and white photography and darkroom techniques combined with independent research in contemporary art and photography. Criticism in contemporary context.

title: History of Photography
description: Artistic, technological, social, and political influences on photography since the early 19th century.

title: Intaglio Printmaking
description: Creative intaglio-etching, drypoint, aquatint, engraving and variations. Emphasis on fine print quality and technical development.

title: Sculpture II
description: Intermediate level investigations into sculptural ideas, processes, and materials.

title: Furniture and Wood II: Joinery Techniques
description: An in-depth exploration of individually driven design, and the joinery techniques required to create unique and durable furniture and objects.

title: Ceramics II - Intermediate Wheel Throwing
description: Investigate intermediate methods of forming, decorating, glazing, and firing vessel forms with an emphasis on the potter’s wheel. Begin developing a conceptual approach to working with clay.

title: Ceramics II - Intermediate Handbuilding
description: Investigate intermediate methods of building, glazing, and firing handbuilt forms. Begin developing a conceptual approach to working with clay.

title: Jewelry and Metalwork II - Fabrication and Color
description: Further development of fabrication skills and coloring techniques to expand technical competence while exploring personal design statements.
notes: Both ART 231 and ART 331 recommended as preparation for this course.

title: Jewelry and Metalwork II - Process and Material
description: Creative design and technical explorations based on contemporary and historical processes and materials.
notes: Both ART 231 and ART 331 recommended as preparation for this course.

title: Digital Photography II
description: Visual and creative expression using digital photographic media with emphasis on refining technical and conceptual visual communication skills.

title: Graphic Design III
description: Analysis and translation of complex information into visual communication systems.

title: Typography III
description: Typographic problem solving including more complex text materials and type with image.

title: Illustration II
description: Drawing and illustration methods, materials, tools, and processes as they relate to art and design.

title: Design for the Internet II
description: Intermediate design and development for World Wide Web. Topics include Web standards, CSS, advanced scripting, and experimental applications.

title: Professional Practice in Art and Design
description: Evolving role of the artist and designer in contemporary art and design practice, standards of professional conduct, and business practices.

title: Graphic Design Internship
description: Field experience with practicing professionals.

title: Senior Portfolio/Exhibition
description: Planning, strategy, and development of a comprehensive body of design work to be professionally presented in a portfolio and/or exhibition format.

title: The Printed Book
description: Creative research focused on concept, context, and form as they relate to communication and personal or collaborative expression within the context of the book.

title: Sequential Media
description: Study and presentation of sequential imagery related to digital video production and motion graphics.

title: Packaging Design
description: Principles and theories of design: branding, typography, illustration, and photography applied to three-dimensional form within a specified social and cultural context with emphasis on strategy and concept; structure, functionality and materials; and modular systems.

title: Residential Design
description: Survey, analysis and conceptual design methods of residential design stressing materials, equipment, components and structural detailing.

title: Art and Design Internship
description: Field experience with practicing professional artists and designers.

title: Construction and Detail Design
description: Approaches to codes and regulations, construction and assembly drawings, contractual agreements, environmental design, project supervision, space planning, and specification writing.

title: Experiential Graphic Design
description: Identification and communication systems applied to environmental solutions. Landmark and wayfinding systems in interior, exterior, and architectural environments.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Advanced Drawing
description: Drawing emphasizing qualitative aspect of visual subject matter.

title: Inter-Media
description: Process and materials in plane and space.

title: Life Drawing and Painting III
description: Drawing and painting from nude and costumed models.

title: Painting III
description: Approaches to contemporary concepts in painting.

title: Contemporary Issues
description: Art and design issues relevant to contemporary global society. Sources of inspiration in art and design practice and topical issues examined. Field trips.

title: Film Photography II
description: Upper-division undergraduate/graduate studio centered around exploring light-sensitive material including 19th-century photographic processes and a “hybrid” analog/digital workflow. Students will expand their disciplinary vocabulary through investigations of photographic history, materiality, and conceptual strategies for developing photographic projects.

title: Sculpture III
description: Advanced level investigations into sculptural ideas, processes, and materials.

title: Figurative Sculpture II
description: Figurative study with emphasis on individual exploration.

title: Tangible Interactivity for Art and Design
description: Introduction to tangible interactivity through an exploration of micro-controller coding, embedding, and wiring into small-scale objects.

title: Furniture and Wood III: Cabinetry
description: Advanced individual design: Exploration of materials, process, and function through exploration of cabinetry and related techniques. Continued focus on development of  specialized techniques.

title: Furniture and Wood III: Seating
description: Advanced individual design: Exploration of materials, process, and function through seating and related techniques. Continued focus on development of specialized techniques.

title: Digital Fabrication for Art and Design
description: Design, visualization, and fabrication processes utilizing modeling and machining software. Basic techniques in computer-aided design (CAD) and computer-aided manufacturing (CAM). Small-scale production techniques and outsourcing for artists and designers.

title: Ceramics III - Advanced Ceramics
description: Advanced methods of creative design and technical exploration based on conceptual development.

title: Clay and Glaze
description: Experimentation with and testing of ceramic materials.

title: Jewelry and Metalwork III - Fabrication and Color
description: Advanced problems involving fabrication and color while exploring personal design statements.

title: Jewelry and Metalwork III - Process and Material
description: Advanced problems involving creative design and technical explorations based on process and materials.

title: Advanced Photographic Projects
description: Visual and creative expression using photographic media, including traditional and digital processes. Emphasis on conceptual project development and portfolio.

title: Graphic Design IV
description: Strategy, planning, and problem solving related to visual communication systems with emphasis on social and cultural context.
